01

How the current application finds content

The shell opens one storage capability, reads the active module registry, and acquires a generation-bound session before loading a domain. Gameplay data and media take separate paths. A package can be installed successfully while a screen fails to consume its data.

The current code still uses SQLite for assets

Your earlier preference was to remove SQLite asset storage. That change is incomplete: native content currently uses Rust/rusqlite; the browser uses SQLite WASM and OPFS. JSON/localStorage is already used for saves and preferences. Tauri does not require SQLite. The proposed filesystem module architecture is described below.

Author & acquire

Tracked recipes and JSON under content/. Ignored card sources/images and chapter media under assets/content/.

Export & stage

content:export produces immutable databases. native:prepare verifies pinned hashes and stages four bundled defaults.

Install & detect

Rust seeds app-data on first launch and commits active.json last. Existing installations are retained and verified on startup.

Query & render

Tauri IPC → read-only rusqlite → semantic adapters → metadata in memory, leased Blob URLs for visible images, preloaded duel Worker data.

Live path on this machine: /home/aron/.local/share/com.ascencio.storyduel/game-content/. Runtime reads <id>-<version>.sqlite selected by active.json.

Build the shell

Vite bundles application code, CSS/fonts, icon and SQLite executable. Native bundled content is a separate resource layer.

Import content

Browser content is selected through the package lifecycle UI. It is independent of the desktop app-data installation.

Activate registry

The content Worker owns SQLite/OPFS and the committed active generation. Dependency validation and session leases protect activation.

Query & render

Worker RPC → TypeScript query implementation → the same semantic adapters. Media uses Blob URL leases; game saves use localStorage.

Opening npm run dev in a browser does not automatically expose the Tauri installation. Browser OPFS and native app-data are separate stores.

The app does not scan arbitrary directories for JPGs. Package IDs, dependencies, versions, active registry entries and logical asset paths determine what it can access.

What “ready” actually checks

  • Exactly one expected default package per ID.
  • Expected package type, schema, version format, file identity, positive byte count and SHA-256 format.
  • Freeplay needs core + library + Freeplay; New Game additionally needs Chapter 01.

Native startup verifies file hashes separately. The menu readiness predicate does not load the chapter into its strict story parser, exercise the screen’s image bindings, or verify the field’s visible rendering.

Why errors look like missing content

A domain acquisition or runtime failure reaches AppShell.recover(). Most failures are mapped to content-invalid and shown as “Content configuration is invalid. Gameplay remains locked.”

A semantic payload mismatch can therefore produce a content warning even when every package is intact. Optional media errors generally degrade to placeholders; missing required engine assets are fatal.

03

Findings for the four reported failures

A1

New Game rejects Chapter 1

Reproduced contract defect

The native set query leaks a storage-only field into a strict story contract.

The browser query returns exactly id, name, releaseYear and cards. Rust deserializes the entire set metadata object and adds cards, retaining imageAssetPath. selectDatedSets() forwards that field, and parseStoryRelease() requires an exact four-key set record. 

Browser set payload → { id, name, releaseYear, cards } → accepted
Native set payload  → { id, name, releaseYear, imageAssetPath, cards }
                    → exact-record validation → STORY_RELEASE_INVALID
                    → shell recovery → content configuration warning

Using the installed databases, the browser shape loads all 75 chapter sets successfully. Reconstructing the Rust payload shape reproduces STORY_RELEASE_INVALID. The native-bridge UI harness reproduces the same content warning in Chromium and WebKit.

Source anchors: src-tauri/src/native_storage.rs, src/storage/runtime/content-query-runtime.ts, src/shell/adapters/sqlite-story-inputs.ts, src/story/ports/parse-story-release.ts, src/story/ports/release-value.ts.

A2

Freeplay deck illustrations are absent

Confirmed wiring defect

The deck tile reads catalog.imageUrl, which is null for every loaded card.

cardsDeckCatalog() maps card metadata without acquiring images. In the actual 14,794-card Freeplay presentation, zero cards have a non-null URL. freePlayDeckTile() still calls the old catalog-based cover helper, and the host does not inject an image-source capability.

Both default decks choose card 97590747 as their first main-deck cover. Its full JPEG (127,686 B) and cropped JPEG (98,527 B) are present and pass the asset reader’s integrity validation. The tile displays its placeholder because it never requests either image.

Source anchors: src/decks/catalog/cards-catalog.ts, src/decks/catalog/ocg-card-mapper.ts, src/shell/screens/free-play-deck-tiles.ts, src/shell/screens/FreePlayMatchSetup.svelte, src/shell/cards/deck-cover.ts.

A3

Freeplay card hover previews have no art

Confirmed wiring defect

Hover rows and the full-preview callback use the same empty metadata URL.

decklistRows() passes croppedCardImageUrl(card?.imageUrl ?? null). cardImageFor() returns catalog.get(code)?.imageUrl ?? null. These paths never call CardImageSource.acquire(), so hovering cannot turn a reference into a visible image.

The fix must acquire a preview when its target changes, cancel obsolete requests, and release its lease when the hover ends or the screen closes. Metadata, names and descriptions can remain synchronous. Cropped image paths must use the variant API; string rewriting a Blob URL cannot select a crop.

Source anchors: src/shell/screens/FreePlayMatchSetup.svelte, src/deck-select/DeckSelectScreen.svelte, src/story/components/CardPreviewHost.svelte (existing lease pattern), src/shell/adapters/sqlite-image-source.ts.

A4

Duel field and hands are clipped in WebKit

Rendering difference reproduced

The 3D board camera paints differently in WebKit, despite valid engine state and nonzero DOM geometry.

The installed engine, scripts and cards produce a successful ready event, public state and a Main Phase prompt. In a 1280 × 800 UI harness, Chromium renders the complete board and both hands. WebKit paints the zones and cards compressed near the bottom, with controls extending beyond the field’s clipped area.

Both engines report a 904 × 663 field slot and roughly identical element rectangles. This separates the problem from package presence and from a missing Worker snapshot. Removing the camera transform temporarily restores visible zones in WebKit, but still clips the opponent’s hand because geometry remains calibrated for the tilted camera. A complete repair must update camera and geometry together.

Show temporary flat-camera diagnostic

04

Proposed repairs and the module direction

P0

Align native and browser semantic contracts · A1

Make Rust’s set query explicitly project the four public fields, matching the TypeScript query. Keep image location in the storage/media layer. Retain strict story validation. Add a native/browser parity test using set metadata that contains imageAssetPath.

Acceptance: native New Game enters Chapter 1; 75 sets load; current saves remain intact; malformed story data still fails validation.

P0

Connect Freeplay to leased image loading · A2 + A3

Pass the session’s existing image capability from the shell into Freeplay setup. Acquire covers for mounted tiles/selected seats and full art for the active preview. Keep leases separate from the metadata catalog; abort stale hover requests and release on change/unmount. Use cropped → full fallback for the broader catalog.

Acceptance: both default covers appear; mouse and keyboard preview show art; rapid hover changes never show the previous card; missing optional images show a placeholder; opening Freeplay does not load all card images.

P0

Repair the camera/geometry path for WebKit · A4

First provide a coherent flat layout: compute geometry with zero tilt, disable the matching camera and hand counter-tilt, and verify both hand bands fit. Then evaluate a single perspective owner for a shared 3D implementation. Do not change CSS projection independently of placement/hit-test math.

Run the actual Linux Tauri/WebKitGTK app at its 820 × 600 minimum, 1280 × 800 and larger sizes. Assert screenshots, visible zones, both hands and a summon/placement action. Chromium-only field acceptance cannot certify the native webview.

Acceptance: zones and hands remain visible after startup and resize; clicks/drop targets match their displayed positions; concealed opponent identities stay hidden.

P1

Separate installed, usable and degraded states

Cache lightweight semantic health results per active generation: configuration parsed, references valid, story release valid, engine loadable. Report optional art coverage separately. Preserve the failing stage and module ID in diagnostics, so a rendering failure does not become a generic content-invalid message.

Audit the remaining catalog-URL consumers, particularly Story shop, reveal, sell and deck selection. Add a native smoke path that exercises New Game, Freeplay cover, hover preview and visible field; a main-menu screenshot is insufficient.

Replace SQLite asset packages with filesystem modules

This follows your stated direction and keeps the existing module registry and game flow contracts. Native modules can be ordinary versioned directories, distributed as archives, verified in staging and activated atomically. Cards and chapter facts continue to use stable IDs. 

game-content/
  active.json                         # active module IDs, versions, hashes
  modules/
    duel-core/1.0.0/
      module.json  config.json  strings/en.json  engine/ocgcore.sync.wasm
    card-library/1.0.0/
      module.json  cards.json  sets.json  scripts/  images/full/  images/cropped/
    freeplay/1.0.0/
      module.json  config.json  decks.json  opponents.json  limits.json
    chapter-01/1.0.0/
      module.json  chapter.json  story.json  decks.json  media/
user-data.json                        # independent mutable saves/preferences

Keep: dependency graphs, module ownership, versioned schemas, generation-bound sessions, stable scene IDs, save-based campaign prerequisites and the CardImageSource interface. Replace: SQLite content readers/exporters with file readers/validators and native resource staging. Optional SQLite for card search would be a disposable, rebuildable index, never the owner of images or saves; start with parsed metadata and an in-memory index and measure whether it is needed.

Native media should use a constrained Tauri asset protocol or bounded binary reads, resolving only paths declared by an active module manifest. Browser support, if retained, can use OPFS files with the same semantic contracts; localStorage remains for user records, not bulk media.

Migration needs its own ADR/build-boundary update: today the app build requires the SQLite WASM executable and forbids content payloads in the frontend. Remove that requirement when all runtime content SQL paths are replaced. Prepare and validate the candidate file modules before switching the active registry; keep user data untouched.

Recommended order

Repair A1–A4 and establish native acceptance first. Then change storage behind the same semantic interfaces. Moving files alone will not repair the empty URL bindings or WebKit’s camera rendering.

Reproduction method

Open installed databases read-only and use the production TypeScript query/runtime adapters. For the native contract, reconstruct the Rust set query’s complete metadata payload from those same databases. Run the actual Vite native-mode UI in Chromium and WebKit with a simulated Tauri invoke bridge serving these read-only data and a temporary in-memory user JSON store.

The UI test reproduces New Game → content configuration warning, Freeplay → empty covers, and Start duel → WebKit camera defect. CSS trials alter only the diagnostic page. This does not measure native IPC throughput or claim a production fix. No application code, installed content, or user save file was modified for this audit.
